greek: Καὶ οὐκ ἠδύνατο Ιωσηφ ἀνέχεσθαι πάντων τῶν παρεστηκότων αὐτῷ, ἀλλʼ εἶπεν Ἐξαποστείλατε πάντας ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ. καὶ οὐ παρειστήκει οὐδεὶς ἔτι τῷ Ιωσηφ, ἡνίκα ἀνεγνωρίζετο τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς αὐτοῦ.
hint: Unable to hold back before his attendants, Joseph sends everyone out and makes himself known to his brothers alone.

notes.text: The middle of ἀνέχω, to bear up against, with the genitive: he could not bear with all those standing by.
LSJ's ἀναγνωρίζω, which cites this verse for the passive; the imperfect, middle or passive: he was making himself known.
Two negatives, οὐ and οὐδείς, strengthen each other: no one at all was standing by.

names.gloss: (Ιωσηφ, from Hebrew Yôsēp̄, which the Hebrew of 30:24 hears in yōsēp̄, "may he add")

greek: καὶ ἀφῆκεν φωνὴν μετὰ κλαυθμοῦ· ἤκουσαν δὲ πάντες οἱ Αἰγύπτιοι, καὶ ἀκουστὸν ἐγένετο εἰς τὸν οἶκον Φαραω.
hint: He weeps aloud; the Egyptians hear, and it is heard in Pharaoh's house.

notes.text: He let go a sound with weeping. The Hebrew has wayyittēn ʾet-qōlô bibkî, he gave his voice in weeping.
κλαυθμός, a weeping, one translation: plain text.
ἀκουστός, heard, audible: it became audible. Hebrew wayyišmaʿ bêt parʿōh, and the house of Pharaoh heard.

reading: and [[sent forth|sent forth, discharged, let go and loose and set free, let go as an aphetos (ἄφετος) and consecrated, let alone and left, gave up and handed over, permitted and allowed|ἀφίημι]] [[sound|sound, tone, sound of the voice, cry, faculty of speech and discourse, language, saying|φωνή]] [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] of weeping; [[heard|heard, had hearing of, heard tell of, knew by hearsay, hearkened and gave ear, listened to and obeyed|ἀκούω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] the [[name:Αἰγύπτιοι]], and [[heard|heard and audible, that should be heard|ἀκουστός]] [[came into being|came to be, arose, was brought into existence|γίνομαι]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[the house|the house, the abode and dwelling, the room and chamber, the house of a god and temple, the household goods and substance, the household and family|οἶκος]] of [[name:Φαραω]].

names.gloss: (Φαραω, from Hebrew Parʿōh, from the Egyptian for "great house")

greek: εἶπεν δὲ Ιωσηφ πρὸς τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοῦ Ἐγώ εἰμι Ιωσηφ· ἔτι ὁ πατήρ μου ζῇ; καὶ οὐκ ἐδύναντο οἱ ἀδελφοὶ ἀποκριθῆναι αὐτῷ· ἐταράχθησαν γάρ.
hint: Joseph reveals who he is and asks whether his father still lives; the brothers are too shaken to answer.

notes.text: The pronoun with εἰμί: I am Joseph.
The aorist passive of ταράσσω, they were stirred up, troubled. The Hebrew has nibhălû mippānāyw, they were dismayed before him.

reading: [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Ιωσηφ]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[the sons of the same mother|the sons of the same mother, the brothers, the near kinsmen|ἀδελφός]] of him I am [[name:Ιωσηφ]]; [[yet|yet, as yet, still, further, besides, moreover|ἔτι]] [[the father|the father, the grandfather|πατήρ]] of me [[lives|lives, is in full life and strength, is fresh and strong|ζάω]]? and not [[were being able|were being able, were capable and strong enough, were powerful and mighty, were having influence, were daring and bearing, were passing for, were worth, were equivalent to, were signifying and meaning, were availing|δύναμαι]] [[the sons of the same mother|the sons of the same mother, the brothers, the near kinsmen|ἀδελφός]] [[to give answer to|to give answer to, to reply, to answer, to answer charges and defend themselves|ἀποκρίνομαι]] to him; [[were stirred|were stirred, were stirred up, were troubled, were confounded and agitated and disturbed and disquieted, were thrown into disorder, were agitated and distracted, were raised by stirring up, were in disorder, were in a state of disorder and anarchy, were shaken in their seat|ταράσσω]] [[for|for, since and as, for otherwise and else, now, but, why and what, would that|γάρ]].

greek: εἶπεν δὲ Ιωσηφ πρὸς τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοῦ Ἐγγίσατε πρός με. καὶ ἤγγισαν. καὶ εἶπεν Ἐγώ εἰμι Ιωσηφ ὁ ἀδελφὸς ὑμῶν, ὃν ἀπέδοσθε εἰς Αἴγυπτον.
hint: He calls them near and tells them he is their brother, the one they sold into Egypt.

notes.text: The aorist middle of ἀποδίδωμι, to give away of one's own will, to sell, as at 37:28.

reading: [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Ιωσηφ]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[the sons of the same mother|the sons of the same mother, the brothers, the near kinsmen|ἀδελφός]] of him [[bring near|bring near, bring up to, approach, be imminent, approximate to, be next of kin, be on the point of|ἐγγίζω]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] me. and [[brought near|brought near, brought up to, approached, were imminent, approximated to, were next of kin, were on the point of|ἐγγίζω]]. and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] I am [[name:Ιωσηφ]] [[the son of the same mother|the son of the same mother, the brother, the near kinsman|ἀδελφός]] of you, whom [[you gave away of your own will|you gave away of your own will, you sold|ἀποδίδωμι]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[name:Αἴγυπτον]].

names.gloss: (Αἴγυπτος, the Greek name of the land; Hebrew Miṣrayim)

greek: νῦν οὖν μὴ λυπεῖσθε μηδὲ σκληρὸν ὑμῖν φανήτω ὅτι ἀπέδοσθέ με ὧδε· εἰς γὰρ ζωὴν ἀπέστειλέν με ὁ θεὸς ἔμπροσθεν ὑμῶν·
hint: They are not to grieve over selling him: God sent him ahead of them to preserve life.

notes.text: Nor let it seem hard to you. The Hebrew has wĕʾal-yiḥar bĕʿênêkem, and let it not burn in your eyes.
ζωή, a living, the means of life: for life, for preserving life. Hebrew lĕmiḥyâ.

greek: τοῦτο γὰρ δεύτερον ἔτος λιμὸς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, καὶ ἔτι λοιπὰ πέντε ἔτη, ἐν οἷς οὐκ ἔσται ἀροτρίασις οὐδὲ ἄμητος·
hint: This is the second year of famine; five more remain without ploughing or harvest.

notes.text: Parsed as an accusative of time, this second year, as MorphGNT reads τοῦτο τρίτον at John 21:14; read as nominatives, this is the second year. Either way λιμός is the subject of the verbless clause.
LSJ's ἀροτρίασις, which points to ἀροτριασμός, ploughing, tillage, and cites this verse.
ἔτος, a year, one translation: plain text.

greek: ἀπέστειλεν γάρ με ὁ θεὸς ἔμπροσθεν ὑμῶν, ὑπολείπεσθαι ὑμῶν κατάλειμμα ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ἐκθρέψαι ὑμῶν κατάλειψιν μεγάλην.
hint: God sent him ahead to keep a remnant for them on the earth and to sustain a great survival.

notes.text: Two nouns of καταλείπω: κατάλειμμα, LSJ's remnant, and κατάλειψις, a leaving behind, each one translation. The Hebrew has šĕʾērît, a remnant, and pĕlêṭâ, an escape.
The present middle infinitive of ὑπολείπω: to leave remaining for yourselves.

reading: [[sent off|sent off, sent away, banished, despatched, went away and departed|ἀποστέλλω]] [[for|for, since and as, for otherwise and else, now, but, why and what, would that|γάρ]] me [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] [[before|before, in front of|ἔμπροσθεν]] of you, [[to leave remaining for oneself|to leave remaining for oneself, to leave behind for oneself, to reserve for oneself|ὑπολείπω]] of you remnant [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + genitive]] [[of the earth|of the earth, of the land, of the ground|γῆ]] and [[to bring up from childhood|to bring up from childhood and rear up|ἐκτρέφω]] of you leaving behind [[big|big, great, tall, full-grown, vast and high, spacious and wide, strong and mighty, violent, loud, prevailing, weighty and important|μέγας]].

greek: νῦν οὖν οὐχ ὑμεῖς με ἀπεστάλκατε ὧδε, ἀλλʼ ἢ ὁ θεός, καὶ ἐποίησέν με ὡς πατέρα Φαραω καὶ κύριον παντὸς τοῦ οἴκου αὐτοῦ καὶ ἄρχοντα πάσης γῆς Αἰγύπτου.
hint: It was God, not they, who sent him, and made him a father to Pharaoh and ruler over all Egypt.

notes.text: ἀλλά with ἤ after a negative: but only, rather.
Φαραω does not decline; the parse takes it as the genitive, a father of Pharaoh. Hebrew lĕʾāb lĕparʿōh, a father to Pharaoh.

greek: σπεύσαντες οὖν ἀνάβητε πρὸς τὸν πατέρα μου καὶ εἴπατε αὐτῷ Τάδε λέγει ὁ υἱός σου Ιωσηφ Ἐποίησέν με ὁ θεὸς κύριον πάσης γῆς Αἰγύπτου· κατάβηθι οὖν πρός με καὶ μὴ μείνῃς·
hint: They are to hurry to their father with Joseph's message: God has made him lord of Egypt; come without delay.

notes.text: ὅδε, this here, in the neuter plural: thus says, introducing the message.
The aorist subjunctive of μένω with μή, a prohibition: do not stay.

[[step down|step down, go and come down, go down from, dismount, come down stairs, go down from the inland parts to the sea, come to land and get safe ashore, go down into the arena, come down from the tribune, come to, end|καταβαίνω]] [[really|really, at all events, surely, so, then and therefore|οὖν]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] me and [[not|not, that not, perhaps, surely not and you don't mean to say that|μή]] [[you may stay stand fast|you may stay stand fast and abide, you may stay at home, you may stay where one is, you may not stir, you may stay away from, you may stay and tarry, you may be lasting and remain and last and stand, you may remain as one was and hold good and remain contented, you may abide by, you may await and expect and wait for|μένω]];

greek: καὶ κατοικήσεις ἐν γῇ Γεσεμ Ἀραβίας καὶ ἔσῃ ἐγγύς μου, σὺ καὶ οἱ υἱοί σου καὶ οἱ υἱοὶ τῶν υἱῶν σου, τὰ πρόβατά σου καὶ αἱ βόες σου καὶ ὅσα σοί ἐστιν,
hint: Jacob will live near Joseph in Gesem of Arabia, with all his family and flocks.

notes.text: In the land of Gesem of Arabia. The Hebrew has bĕʾereṣ-gōšen, in the land of Goshen; Ἀραβίας is the Greek's.
βοῦς feminine, with αἱ: the cows. The chain is the word's, whose first sense is bullocks.

reading: and [[you will dwell in as a katoikos (κάτοικος)|you will dwell in as a katoikos (κάτοικος), you will settle in, you will colonise, you will inhabit, you will settle and dwell, you will lie and be situate|κατοικέω]] [[in earth|within, inside of, and by means of earth, land, ground|ἐν; γῆ]] of [[name:Γεσεμ]] of [[name:Ἀραβίας]] and you will be [[hard by|hard by, near to, near, nigh, at hand, nigh at hand, nearly, akin to|ἐγγύς]] of me, you and the sons of you and the sons of the sons of you, [[the things that walk forward|the things that walk forward, the cattle, the flocks and herds, the horses, the small cattle, the sheep|πρόβατον]] of you and [[the bullocks|the bullocks and bulls and oxen, the cows, the oxen, the kine and cattle, the ox-hide shields|βοῦς]] of you and [[as great as|as great as, as much as, as far as, as long as, as many as|ὅσος]] to you is,

names.gloss: (Γεσεμ, from Hebrew Gōšen, of uncertain meaning)
(Ἀραβία, the Greek name of the land of the Ἄραβες, the Arabs)

greek: καὶ ἐκθρέψω σε ἐκεῖ — ἔτι γὰρ πέντε ἔτη λιμός —, ἵνα μὴ ἐκτριβῇς, σὺ καὶ οἱ υἱοί σου καὶ πάντα τὰ ὑπάρχοντά σου.
hint: He will provide for them through the five remaining years of famine, so they are not ruined.

notes.text: Rahlfs sets the clause between dashes; the reading carries them as parentheses. πέντε ἔτη is parsed as the accusative of duration.
The aorist passive subjunctive of ἐκτρίβω, to rub out: lest you be rubbed out. The Hebrew has pen-tiwwārēš, lest you come to poverty.

reading: and [[I will bring up from childhood|I will bring up from childhood and rear up|ἐκτρέφω]] you [[there|there, in that place|ἐκεῖ]] ([[yet|yet, as yet, still, further, besides, moreover|ἔτι]] [[for|for, since and as, for otherwise and else, now, but, why and what, would that|γάρ]] five years [[hunger|hunger, famine|λιμός]]), [[that|that, in order that|ἵνα]] [[not|not, that not, perhaps, surely not and you don't mean to say that|μή]] [[you may be rubbed out|you may be rubbed out, you may be rubbed hard, you may be destroyed root and branch, you may be rubbed constantly and worn out|ἐκτρίβω]], you and the sons of you and [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] [[the existing circumstances|the existing circumstances, the present advantages, the what belongs to one, the possessions and means|ὑπάρχω]] of you.

greek: ἰδοὺ οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ ὑμῶν βλέπουσιν καὶ οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ Βενιαμιν τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ μου ὅτι τὸ στόμα μου τὸ λαλοῦν πρὸς ὑμᾶς.
hint: Their own eyes and Benjamin's see that it is Joseph's own mouth speaking to them.

notes.text: A verbless clause after ὅτι: that my mouth is the one speaking to you. The participle's article is neuter, with στόμα: the thing talking.

reading: [[lo|lo, behold, see there|ἰδού]] [[the eyes|the eyes, the dearest and best, the comfort, the buds|ὀφθαλμός]] of you [[see|see and have the power of sight, look, look longingly and expect eagerly, look to, beware of, see that, see and behold, see the light of day and live, are alive and live|βλέπω]] and [[the eyes|the eyes, the dearest and best, the comfort, the buds|ὀφθαλμός]] of [[name:Βενιαμιν]] [[of the son of the same mother|of the son of the same mother, of the brother, of the near kinsman|ἀδελφός]] of me [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] [[the mouth|the mouth, the mouth as the organ of speech, the mouthpiece, the face, the chasm and cleft|στόμα]] of me [[the thing talking|the thing talking, the thing chatting, the thing prattling, the thing babbling, the thing saying, the thing talking of, the thing speaking, the thing chattering, the thing chirping|λαλέω]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] you.

names.gloss: (Βενιαμιν, from Hebrew Binyāmîn, "son of the right hand" or "son of the south")

greek: ἀπαγγείλατε οὖν τῷ πατρί μου πᾶσαν τὴν δόξαν μου τὴν ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ καὶ ὅσα εἴδετε, καὶ ταχύναντες καταγάγετε τὸν πατέρα μου ὧδε.
hint: They are to tell their father of Joseph's glory in Egypt and bring him down quickly.

notes.lemma: τὴν δόξαν μου τὴν ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ
notes.text: δόξα, whose first sense is a notion, an opinion, and which runs to glory and splendour: my glory, the glory in Egypt.
The aorist participle of ταχύνω, to make haste: hurrying.

greek: καὶ ἐπιπεσὼν ἐπὶ τὸν τράχηλον Βενιαμιν τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ ἔκλαυσεν ἐπʼ αὐτῷ, καὶ Βενιαμιν ἔκλαυσεν ἐπὶ τῷ τραχήλῳ αὐτοῦ.
